report: Mit 3 mm grenzwertige Extrusion des Innenmeniskus bei komplexem Riss des Hinterhorns und der Pars intermedia mit horizontaler, radiärer und vertikaler Komponente (exemplarisch 7/13). Dorsomedial betonte, flächige, nicht-vollschichtige Ausdünnung des Knorpels im medialen Kompartiment. Fokal zwei vollschichtige chondrale Risse auf Höhe der Pars intermedia des Innenmeniskus (6/12) mit begleitendem Knochenmarksödem (1010/36). Geringe Signalanhebung des Außenmeniskus, insbesondere am Hinterhorn (6/28). Zeichen einer Reizsynovialitis bei betonter Synovia. Plica mediopatellaris. Geringer Gelenkerguss. Enthesophyten am Quadrizepssehnenansatz. Signalanhebung der Sehne am Patellasehnenursprung (7/24). Geringe Flüssigkeitskollektion ventral des Lig. patellae (3/102).

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia izquierda.
Hallazgos:
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Aumento de señal central del del cuerpo, cuerno posterior del menisco medial que no impresiona
contactar con la superficie articular.
Menisco lateral con rotura degenerativa marginal del cuerno anterior y parte del cuerpo, sin
desplazamiento de segmentos.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de distribución difusa los compartimentos femorotibiales de
predominio medial. Pequeña formación quística subcortical de 2 mm periférica del platillo tibial
medial, reactiva.
Prácticamente ausencia de visualización del cartílago patelofemoral de distribución difusa con
formaciones quísticas subcorticales.
Moderado derrame articular con sinovitis difusa.
Cambios entesopáticos cuadricipitales distales. Tendón rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso,
bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Discreto edema las partes blandas profundo a los tendones de la pata de ganso en su región
distal.
Impresión:
Signos de una rotura marginal del cuerno anterior y parte del cuerpo del menisco lateral.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 y 3 de los compartimentos femorotibiales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 4 distribución difusa de la articulación patelofemoral con importantes
cambios óseos secundarios.
Moderado derrame articular con sinovitis difusa.
Cambios entesopáticos cuadricipitales distales.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:Right knee lateral pain gradual onset, pain in patellar tendon and lateral posterior knee as well, positive McMurray very test, rule out meniscal tear, also suspicious for hamstring tendinitis/patellar tendinitis.

PRIOR IMAGING: None available.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanisms are intact; the patellar tendon is homogenously hypointense without evidence of inflammation. The patellar cartilage at the facet of the lateral femoral condyle appears enlarged with heterogenous enhancement consistent with low-grade/grade I chondromalacia patella. The trochlear cartilage is intact. Visualized hamstring tendons of the biceps for Morris, semitendinosus and semimembranosus appear unremarkable. The patellar soft tissues are normal.

The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits.

The anterior cruciate, posterior cruciate, medial collateral and lateral collateral stabilizes, fibular collateral collateral ligament, popliteus, biceps femoris tendon and iliotibial tendons, appear intact. No measurable anterior tibial translation.

Lateral and medial menisci appears intact. Articular cartilage of the lateral and medial femoral condyles are intact.

Small knee joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Marrow signal normal. 

INTERPRETATION: 
Mild chondromalacia of the lateral patellar femoral condyle facet.

Patellar tendon and biceps femoris tendons appear unremarkable, without evidence of tendinitis.

Focal increased signal intensity in subchondral region of posterior medial femoral condyle and fibular head on F/S T2WI, R/O intraosseous hemangioma; differential diagnosis of focal bone marrow edema.
Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.

> The contour of ACL in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1 injury or degeneration and synovial interposition.

> No evidence of tear is noted in either medial or lateral meniscus.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Mild subcutanoeus edema over right knee.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of right knee with grade 3-4 chondromalacia.
2. R/O intraosseous hemangioma in right posterior medial femoral condyle and right fibular head (Srs/Img: [ID]; differential diagnosis of bone marrow edema.
3. Moderate synovitis- joint effsuion  of right knee.
4. R/O grade 1 injury or degeneration of ACL; differential diagnosis of synovial interposition over distal ACL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: r/o medial meniscal tear; medial right knee pain with bending, prior skiing injury a long time ago 
Comparison: Knee radiographs [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Trace joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Maceration of the body of the medial meniscus with moderate extrusion and displacement toward the meniscofemoral recess.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the weightbearing medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness loss along the weightbearing lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness cartilage loss along the medial and lateral facet with underlying subchondral edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Maceration of the body of the medial meniscus with moderate extrusion and displacement toward the meniscofemoral recess.
2.	Mild tricompartmental chondrosis, most significant in the patellofemoral compartment.
3.	Small Baker's cyst.
